verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dyaus quickens and promotes your high dominion who bind with bonds not wrought of rope or cordage. Far from us still be Varuna's displeasure may Indra give us spacious room to dwell in.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Make ye our sacrifice fair amid the assemblies: make ye our prayers approved among our princes. May God-sent riches come for our possession: further ye us with your delightful succours.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra-Varuna, vouchsafe us riches with store of treasure, food, and every blessing; For the Aditya, banisher of falsehood, the Hero, dealeth wealth in boundless plenty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this my song reach Varuna and Indra, and, strongly urging, win me sons and offspring. To the Gods' banquet may we go with riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR you I deck a harmless hymn, presenting the Soma juice to Varuna and Indra- A hymn that shines like heavenly Dawn with fatness. May they be near us on the march and guard us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here where the arrows fall amid the banners both hosts invoke the Gods in emulation. O Indra-Varuna, smite back those-our foemen, yea, smite them with your shaft to every quarter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Self-lucid in their seats, e'en heavenly Waters endowed with Godhead Varuna and Indra. One of these holds the folk distinct and sundered, the Other smites and slays resistless foemen.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise be the priest and skilled in Law Eternal, who with his sacred gifts and oration. Brings you to aid us with your might, Adityas: let him have viands to promote his welfare.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this my song reach Varuna and Indra, and, strongly urging, win me sons and offspring. To the Gods' banquet may we go with riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WISE, verily, are creatures through his greatness who stayed ever, spacious heaven and earth asunder; Who urged the high and mighty sky to motion, the Star of old, and spread the earth before him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With mine own heart I commune on the question how Varuna and I may be united. What gift of mine will he accept unangered? When may I calmly look and find him gracious?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Fain to know this in I question others: I seek the wise, O Varuna, and ask them. This one same answer even the sages gave me, "Surely this Varuna is angry with thee."
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What, Varuna, hath been my chief transgression, that thou wouldst slay the friend who sings thy praises? Tell me, Unconquerable Lord, and quickly sinless will I approach thee with mine homage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Free us from sins committed by our fathers, from those wherein we have ourselves offended. O King, loose, like a thief who feeds the cattle, as from the cord a calf, set free Vasistha.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Not our own will betrayed us, but seduction, thoughtlessness, Varuna wine, dice, or anger. The old is near to lead astray the younger: even sleep removeth not all evil-doing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slave like may I do service to the Bounteous, serve, free from sin, the God inclined to anger. This gentle Lord gives wisdom to the simple: the wiser God leads on the wise to riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Lord, O Varuna, may this laudation come close to them and lie within thy spirit. May it be well with us in rest and labour. Preserve us ever-more, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: VARUNA cut a pathway out for Surya, and led the watery floods of rivers onward. The Mares, as in a race, speed on in order. He made great channels for the days to follow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The wind, thy breath, hath sounded through the region like a wild beast that seeks his food in pastures. Within these two, exalted Earth and Heaven, O Varuna, are all the forms thou lovest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Varuna's spies, sent forth upon their errand, survey the two world-halves well formed and fashioned. Wise are they, holy, skilled in sacrifices, the furtherers of the praise-songs of the prudent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To me who understand hath Varuna spoken, the names borne by the Cow are three times seven. The sapient God, knowing the place's secret, shall speak as 'twere to teach the race that cometh.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On him three heavens rest and are supported, and the three earths are there in sixfold order. The wise King Varuna hath made in heaven that Golden Swing to cover it with glory.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Varuna from heaven he sinks in Sindhu, like a white-shining spark, a strong wild creature. Ruling in depths and meting out the region, great saving power hath he, this world's Controller.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Before this Varuna may we be sinless him who shows mercy even to the sinner- While we are keeping Aditi's ordinances. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: PRESENT to Varuna thine hymn, Vasistha, bright, most delightful to the Bounteous Giver, Who bringeth on to us the Bull, the lofty, the Holy, laden with a thousand treasures.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And now, as I am come before his presence, I take the face of Varuna for Agni's. So might he bring-Lord also of the darkness-the light in heaven that I may see its beauty!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Varuna and I embark together and urge our boat into the midst of ocean, We, when we ride o'er ridges of the waters, will swing within that swing and there be happy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Varuna placed Vasistha in the vessel, and deftly with his night made him a Rsi. When days shone bright the Sage made him a singer, while the heavens broadened and the Dawns were lengthened.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What hath become of those our ancient friendships, when without enmity we walked together? I, Varuna, thou glorious Lord, have entered thy lofty home, thine house with thousand portals.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If he, thy true ally, hath sinned against thee, still, Varuna, he is the friend thou lovest. Let us not, Living One, as sinners I know thee: give shelter, as a Sage, to him who lauds thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While we abide in these fixed habitations, and from the lap of Aditi win favour, May Varuna untie the bond that binds us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: LET me not yet, King Varuna, enter into the house of clay: Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Thunderer! I move along tremulous like a wind-blown skin, Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Bright and Powerful God, through want of strength I erred and went astray Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thirst found thy worshipper though he stood in the midst of water-fjords: Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Varuna, whatever the offence may be which we as men commit against the heavenly host, When through our want of thought we violate thy laws, punish us not, O God, for that iniquity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To you pure juice, rich in meath, are offered by priest: through longing for the Pair of Heroes. Drive, Vayu, bring thine harnessed horses hither: drink the pressed Soma till it make thee joyful.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso to thee, the Mighty, brings oblation, pure Soma unto thee, pure-drinking Vayu, That man thou makest famous among mortals: to him strong sons are born in quick succession.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The God whom both these worlds brought forth for riches, whom heavenly Dhisana for our wealth appointeth, His team of harnessed horses waits on Vayu, and, foremost, on the radiant Treasure-bearer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The spotless Dawns with fair bright days have broken; they found the spacious light when they were shining. Eagerly they disclosed the stall of cattle: floods streamed for them as in the days aforetime.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These with their truthful spirit, shining brightly, move on provided with their natural insight. Viands attend the car that beareth Heroes, your car, ye Sovran Pair, Indra and Vayu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May these who give us heavenly light, these rulers, with gifts of kine and horses, gold and treasures. These princes, through full life, Indra and Vayu! o'ercome in battle with their steeds and heroes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like coursers seeking fame will we Vasisthas, O Indra-Vayu, with our fair laudations. Exerting all our power call you to aid us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WERE not in sooth, the Gods aforetime blameless, whose pleasure was increased by adoration? For Vayu and for man in his affliction they caused the Morning to arise with Surya.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Guardians infallible, eager as envoys' preserve us safe through many months and autumns. Addressed to you, our fair praise, Indra-Vayu, implores your favour and renewed well-being.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wise, bright, arranger of his teams, he. seeketh men with rich food whose treasures are abundant. They have arranged them of one mind with Vayu: the men have wrought all noble operations.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So far as native power and strength permit you, so far as men behold whose eyes have vision, O ye pure-drinkers, drink with us pure Soma: sit on this sacred grass, Indra and Vayu.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Driving down teams that bear the lovely Heroes, hitherward, Indra-Vayu, come together. To you this prime of savoury juice is offered: here loose your horses and be friendly-minded.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Your hundred and your thousand teams, O Indra and Vayu, all-munificent, which attend you, With these most gracious-minded come ye hither, and drink, O Heroes of the meath we offer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like coursers seeking fame will we Vasisthas, O Indra-Vayu, with our fair laudations, Exerting all our power, call you to aid us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O VAYU, drinker of the pure, be near us: a thousand teams are thine, Allbounteous Giver. To thee the rapture-bringing juice is offered, whose first draught, God, thou takest as thy portion.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prompt at the holy rites forth came the presser with Soma-draughts for Indra and for Vayu, When ministering priests with strong devotion bring to you Twain the first taste of the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The teams wherewith thou seekest him who offers, within his home, O Vayu, to direct him, Therewith send wealth: to us with full enjoyment, a hero son and gifts of kine and horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Near to the Gods and making Indra joyful, devout and offering precious gifts to Vayu, Allied with princes, smiting down the hostile, may we with heroes conquer foes in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With thy yoked teams in hundreds and in thousands come to our sacrifice and solemn worship. Come, Vayu, make thee glad at this libation. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SLAYERS of enemies, Indra and Agni, accept this day our new-born pure laudation. Again, again I call you prompt to listen, best to give quickly strength to him who craves it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For ye were strong to gain, exceeding mighty, growing together, waxing in your vigour. Lords of the pasture filled with ample riches, bestow upon us strength both fresh and lasting.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yea when the strong have entered our assembly, and singers seeking with their hymns your favour, They are like steeds who come into the race-course, those men who call aloud on Indra-Agni.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The singer, seeking with his hymns your favour, begs splendid riches of their first possessor. Further us with new bounties, Indra-Agni, armed with strong thunder, slayers of the foeman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When two great hosts, arrayed against each other, meet clothed with brightness, in the fierce encounter Stand ye beside the godly, smite the godless; and still assist the men who press the Soma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To this our Soma-pressing, Indra-Agni, come ye prepared to show your loving-kindness, For not at any time have ye despised us. So may I draw you with all strengthenings hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So Agni, kindled mid this adoration, invite thou Mitra, Varuna, and Indra. Forgive whatever sin we have committed may Aryaman and Aditi remove it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While we accelerate these our sacrifices, may we win strength from both of you, O Agni: Ne'er may the Maruts, Indra, Visnu slight us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As rain from out the cloud, for you, Indra and Agni, from my soul This noblest praise hath been produced.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Do ye, O Indra-Agni, hear the singer's call: accept his songs. Ye Rulers, grant his heart's desire.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us not up to poverty, ye Heroes, Indra-Agni, nor To slander and reproach of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Indra and to Agni we bring reverence, high and holy hymn, And, craving help, soft words with prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For all these holy singers here implore these Twain to succour them, And priests that they may win them strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Eager to laud you, we with songs invoke you, bearing sacred food, Fain for success in sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Agni, come to us with favour, ye who conquer men: Let not the wicked master us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: At no time let the injurious blow of hostile mortal fall on us: O Indra-Agni, shelter us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whatever wealth we crave of you, in gold, in cattle, or in steeds, That, Indra-Agni, let us gain;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When heroes prompt in worship call Indra and Agni, Lords of steeds, Beside the Soma juice effused.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Call hither with the song and lauds those who best slay the foemen, those Who take delight in hymns of praise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slay ye the wicked man whose thought is evil of the demon kind. Slay him who stays the waters, slay the Serpent with your deadly dart.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS stream Sarasvati with fostering current comes forth, our sure defense, our fort of iron. As on a car, the flood flows on, surpassing in majesty and might all other waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pure in her course from mountains to the ocean, alone of streams Sarasvati hath listened. Thinking of wealth and the great world of creatures, she poured for Nahusa her milk and fatness.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Friendly to man he grew among the women, a strong young Steer amid the Holy Ladies. He gives the fleet steed to our wealthy princes, and decks their bodies for success in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this Sarasvati be pleased and listen at this our sacrifice, auspicious Lady, When we with reverence, on our knees, implore her close-knit to wealth, most kind to those she loveth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These offerings have ye made with adoration: say this, Sarasvati, and accept our praises; And, placing us under thy dear protection, may we approach thee, as a tree, for shelter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For thee, O Blest Sarasvati, Vasistha hath here unbarred the doors d sacred Order. Wax, Bright One, and give strength to him who lauds thee. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I SING a lofty song, for she is mightiest, most divine of Streams. Sarasvati will I exalt with hymns and lauds, and, O Vasistha, Heaven and Earth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When in the fulness of their strength the Purus dwell, Beauteous One, on thy two grassy banks, Favour us thou who hast the Maruts for thy friends: stir up the bounty of our chiefs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may Sarasvati auspicious send good luck; she, rich in spoil, is never niggardly in thought, When praised in Jamadagni's way and lauded as Vasistha lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We call upon Sarasvan, as unmarried men who long for wives, As liberal men who yearn for sons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be thou our kind protector, O Sarasvan, with those waves of thine Laden with sweets and dropping oil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we enjoy Sarasvan's breast, all-beautiful, that swells with streams, May we gain food and progeny.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHERE Heaven and Earth combine in men's assembly, and those who love the Gods delight in worship, Where the libations are effused for Indra, may he come first to drink and make him stronger.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We crave the heavenly grace of Gods to guard us-so may Brhaspati, O friends, exalt us- That he, the Bounteous God, may find us sinless, who giveth from a distance like a father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That Brahmanaspati, most High and Gracious, I glorify with offerings and with homage. May the great song of praise divine, reach Indra who is the King of prayer the Gods' creation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May that Brhaspati who brings all blessings, most dearly loved, be seated by our altar. Heroes and wealth we crave; may he bestow them, and bear us safe beyond the men who vex us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To us these Deathless Ones, erst born, have granted this laud of ours which gives the Immortal pleasure. Let us invoke Brhaspati, the foeless, the clear-voiced God, the Holy One of households
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Him, this Brhaspati, his red-hued horses, drawing together, full of strength, bring hither. Robed in red colour like the cloud, they carry the Lord of Might whose friendship gives a dwelling.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For he is pure, with hundred wings, refulgent, with sword of gold, impetuous, winning sunlight. Sublime Brhaspati, easy of access granteth his friends most bountiful refreshment.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Both Heaven and Earth, divine, the Deity's Parents, have made Brhaspati increase in grandeur. Glorify him, O friends, who merits glory: may he give prayer fair way and easy passage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This, Brahmanaspati, is your laudation prayer hath been made to thunder wielding Indra. Favour our songs, wake up our thought and spirit: destroy the godless and our foemen's malice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Twain are Lords of wealth in earth and heaven, thou, O Brhaspati, and thou, O Indra. Mean though he be, give wealth to him who lauds you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: PRIESTS, offer to the Lord of all the people the milked-out stalk of Soma, radiant-coloured. No wild-bull knows his drinking-place like Indra who ever seeks him who hath pressed the Soma,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou dost desire to drink, each day that passes, the pleasant food which thou hast had aforetime, O Indra, gratified in heart and spirit, drink eagerly the Soma set before thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, newly-born, for strength didst drink the Soma; the Mother told thee of thy future greatness. O Indra, thou hast filled mid-air's wide region, and given the Gods by battle room and freedom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When thou hast urged the arrogant to combat, proud in their strength of arm, we will subdue them. Or, Indra, when thou fightest girt by heroes, we in the glorious fray with thee will conquer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I will declare the earliest deeds of Indra, and recent acts which Maghavan hath accomplished. When he had conquered godless wiles and magic, Soma became his own entire possession.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thine is this world of flocks and herds around thee, which with the eye of Surya thou beholdest. Thou, Indra, art alone the Lord of cattle; may we enjoy the treasure which thou givest.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Twain are Lords of wealth in earth and heaven, thou, O Brhaspati, and thou, O Indra. Mean though he be, give wealth to him who lauds you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MEN come not nigh thy majesty who growest beyond all bound and measure with thy body. Both thy two regions of the earth, O Visnu, we know: thou God, knowest the highest also.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: None who is born or being born, God Visnu, hath reached the utmost limit of thy grandeur. The vast high vault of heaven hast thou supported, and fixed earth's eastern pinnacle securely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich in sweet food be ye, and rich in milch-kine, with fertile pastures, fain to do men service. Both these worlds, Visnu, hast thou stayed asunder, and firmly fixed the earth with pegs around it.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye have made spacious room for sacrificing by generating Surya, Dawn, and Agni. O Heroes, ye have conquered in your battles even the bull-jawed Dasa's wiles and magic.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye have destroyed, thou, Indra, and thou Visnu, Sambara's nine-and-ninety fenced castles. Ye Twain smote down a hundred times a thousand resistless heroes of the royal Varcin.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This is the lofty hymn of praise, exalting the Lords of Mighty Stride, the strong and lofty. I laud you in the solemn synods, Visnu: pour ye food on us in our camps, O Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Visnu, unto thee my lips cry Vasat! Let this mine offering, Sipivista, please thee. May these my songs of eulogy exalt thee. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: NE'ER doth the man repent, who, seeking profit, bringeth his gift to the far-striding Visnu. He who adoreth him with all his spirit winneth himself so great a benefactor.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, Visnu, constant in thy courses, gavest good-will to all men, and a hymn that lasteth, That thou mightst move us to abundant comfort of very splendid wealth with store of horses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three times strode forth this God in all his grandeur over this earth bright with a hundred splendours. Foremost be Visnu, stronger than the strongest: for glorious is his name who lives for ever.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Over this earth with mighty step strode Visnu, ready to give it for a home to Manu. In him the humble people trust for safety: he, nobly born, hath made them spacious dwellings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To-day I laud this name, O gipivista, I, skilled in rules, the name of thee the Noble. Yea, I the poor and weak praise thee the Mighty who dwellest in the realm beyond this region.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What was there to be blamed in thee, O Visnu, when thou declaredst, I am Sipivista? Hide not this form from us, nor keep it secret, since thou didst wear another shape in battle.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Visnu, unto thee my lips cry Vasat! Let this mine offering, Sipivista, please thee. May these my songs of eulogy exalt thee. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SPEAK forth three words, the words which light precedeth, which milk this udder that produceth nectar. Quickly made manifest, the Bull hath bellowed, engendering the germ of plants, the Infant.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Giver of growth to plants, the God who ruleth over the waters and all moving creatures, Vouchsafe us triple shelter for our refuge, and threefold light to succour and befriend us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now he is sterile, now begetteth offspring, even as he willeth doth he change his figure. The Father's genial flow bedews the Mother; therewith the Sire, therewith the son is nourished.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In him all living creatures have their being, and the three heavens with triply flowing waters. Three reservoirs that sprinkle down their treasure shed their sweet streams around him with a murmur.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this my song to Sovran Lord Parjanya come near unto his heart and give him pleasure. May we obtain the showers that bring enjoyment, and God-protected plants with goodly fruitage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He is the Bull of all, and their impregner lie holds the life of all things fixed and moving. May this rite save me till my hundredth autumn. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: SING forth and laud Parjanya, son of Heaven, who sends the gift of rain May he provide our pasturage.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Parjanya is the God who forms in kine, in mares, in plants of earth, And womankind, the germ of life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Offer and pour into his mouth oblation rich in savoury juice: May he for ever give us food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THEY who lay quiet for a year, the Brahmans who fulfil their vows, The Frogs have lifted up their voice, the voice Parjanya hath inspired.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time on these, as on a dry skin lying in the pool's bed, the floods of heaven descended, The music of the Frogs comes forth in concert like the cows lowing with their calves beside them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When at the coming of the Rains the water has poured upon them as they yearned and thirsted, One seeks another as he talks and greets him with cries of pleasure as a son his father.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Each of these twain receives the other kindly, while they are revelling in the flow of waters, When the Frog moistened by the rain springs forward, and Green and Spotty both combine their voices.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When one of these repeats the other's language, as he who learns the lesson of the teacher, Your every limb seems to be growing larger as ye converse with eloquence on the waters.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Onc is Cow-bellow and Goat-bleat the other, one Frog is Green and one of them is Spotty. They bear one common name, and yet they vary, and, talking, modulate the voice diversely.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As Brahmans, sitting round the brimful vessel, talk at the Soma-rite of Atiratra, So, Frogs, ye gather round the pool to honour this day of all the year, the first of Rain-time.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These Brahmans with the Soma juice, performing their year-long rite, have lifted up their voices; And these Adhvaryus, sweating with their kettles, come forth and show themselves, and none are hidden.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They keep the twelve month's God-appointed order, and never do the men neglect the season. Soon as the Rain-time in the year returneth, these who were heated kettles gain their freedom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Cow-bellow and Goat-bleat have granted riches, and Green and Spotty have vouchsafed us treasure. The Frogs who give us cows in hundreds lengthen our lives in this most fertilizing season.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: INDRA and Soma, burn, destroy the demon foe, send downward, O ye Bulls, those who add gloom to gloom. Annihilate the fools, slay them and burn them up: chase them away from us, pierce the voracious ones.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Soma, let sin round the wicked boil like as a caldron set amid the flames of fire. Against the foe of prayer, devourer of raw flesh, the vile fiend fierce of eye, keep ye perpetual hate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Soma, plunge the wicked in the depth, yea, cast them into darkness that hath no support, So that not one of them may ever thence return: so may your wrathful might prevail and conquer them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Soma, hurl your deadly crushing bolt down on the wicked fiend from heaven and from the earth. Yea, forge out of the mountains your celestial dart wherewith ye burn to death the waxing demon race.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Soma, cast ye downward out of heaven your deadly darts of stone burning with fiery flame, Eternal, scorching darts; plunge the voracious ones within the depth, and let them sink without a sound.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra and Soma, let this hymn control you both, even as the girth encompasses two vigorous steeds- The song of praise which I with wisdom offer you: do ye, as Lords of men, animate these my prayers.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In your impetuous manner think ye both thereon: destroy these evil beings, slay the treacherous fiends. Indra and Soma, let the wicked have no bliss who evermore assails us with malignity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whoso accuses me with words of falsehood when I pursue my way with guileless spirit, May he, the speaker of untruth, be, Indra, like water which the hollowed hand compresses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those who destroy, as is their wont, the simple, and with their evil natures harm the righteous, May Soma give them over to the serpent, or to the lap of Nirrti consign them.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fiend, O Agni, who designs to injure the essence of our food, kine, steeds, or bodies, May he, the adversary, thief, and robber, sink to destruction, both himself and offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he be swept away, himself and children: may all the three earths press him down beneath them. May his fair glory, O ye Gods, be blighted, who in the day or night would fain destroy us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The prudent finds it easy to distinguish the true and false: their words oppose each other. Of these two that which is the true and honest, Soma protects, and brings the false to nothing.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Never doth Soma aid and guide the wicked or him who falsely claims the Warrior's title. He slays the fiend and him who speaks untruly: both lie entangled in the noose of Indra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As if I worshipped deities of falsehood, or thought vain thoughts about the Gods, O Agni. Why art thou angry with us, Jatavedas? Destruction fall on those who lie against thee!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So may I die this day if I have harassed any man's life or if I be a demon. Yea, may he lose all his ten sons together who with false tongue hath called me Yatudhana.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Indra slay him with a mighty weapon, and let the vilest of all creatures perish, The fiend who says that he is pure, who calls me a demon though devoid of demon nature.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: She too who wanders like an owl at night-time, hiding her body in her guile and malice, May she fall downward into endless caverns. May press-stones with loud ring destroy the demons.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Spread out, ye Maruts, search among the people: seize ye and grind the Raksasas to pieces, Who fly abroad, transformed to birds, at night-time, or sully and pollute our holy worship.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hurl down from heaven thy bolt of stone, O Indra: sharpen it, Maghavan, made keen by Soma. Forward, behind, and from above and under, smite down the demons with thy rocky weapon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They fly, the demon dogs, and, bent on mischief, fain would they harm indomitable Indra. Sakra makes sharp his weapon for the wicked: now, let him cast his bolt at fiendish wizards.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra hath ever been the fiends' destroyer who spoil oblations of the Gods' invokers: Yea, Sakra, like an axe that splits the timber, attacks and smashes them like earthen vessels.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Destroy the fiend shaped like an owl or owlet, destroy him in the form of dog or cuckoo. Destroy him shaped as eagle or as vulture as with a stone, O Indra, crush the demon.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the fiend of witchcraft-workers reach us: may Dawn drive off the couples of Kimidins. Earth keep us safe from earthly woe and trouble: from grief that comes from heaven mid-air preserve us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slay the male demon, Indra! slay the female, joying and triumphing in arts of magic. Let the fools' gods with bent necks fall and perish, and see no more the Sun when he arises.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Look each one hither, look around Indra and Soma, watch ye well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GLORIFY naught besides, O friends; so shall no sorrow trouble you. Praise only mighty Indra when the juice is shed, and say your lauds repeatedly:
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even him, eternal, like a bull who rushes down, men's Conqueror, bounteous like a cow; Him who is cause of both, of enmity and peace, to both sides most munificent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Although these men in sundry ways invoke thee to obtain thine aid, Be this our prayer, addressed, O Indra, unto thee, thine exaltation every day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those skilled in song, O Maghavan among these men o'ercome with might the foeman's songs. Come hither, bring us strength in many a varied form most near that it may succour us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Caster of the Stone, I would not sell thee for a mighty price, Not for a thousand, Thunderer! nor ten thousand, nor a hundred, Lord of countless wealth!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, thou art more to me than sire or niggard brother is. Thou and my mother, O Good Lord, appear alike, to give me wealth abundantly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where art thou? Whither art thou gone? For many a place attracts thy mind. Haste, Warrior, Fort-destroyer, Lord of battle's din, haste, holy songs have sounded forth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sing out the psalm to him who breaks down castles for his faithful friend, Verses to bring the Thunderer to destroy the forts and sit on Kanva's sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Horses which are thine in tens, in hundreds, yea, in thousands thine, Even those vigorous Steeds, fleet-footed in the course, with those come quickly near to us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This day I call Sabardugiha who animates the holy song, Indra the richly-yielding Milch-cow who provides unfailing food in ample stream.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When Sura wounded Etasa, with Vata's rolling winged car. Indra bore Kutsa Arjuneya off, and mocked Gandharva. the unconquered One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He without ligature, before making incision in the neck, Closed up the wound again, most wealthy Maghavan, who maketh whole the injured part.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May we be never cast aside, and strangers, as it were, to thee. We, Thunder-wielding Indra, count ourselves as trees rejected and unfit to burn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Vrtra-slayer, we were thought slow and unready for the fray. Yet once in thy great bounty may we have delight, O Hero, after praising thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If he will listen to my laud, then may out Soma-drops that flow Rapidly through the strainer gladden Indra, drops due to the Tugryas' Strengthener.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come now unto the common laud of thee and of thy faithful friend. So may our wealthy nobles' praise give joy to thee. Fain would I sing thine eulogy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Press out the Soma with the stones, and in the waters wash it clean. The men investing it with raiment made of milk shall milk it forth from out the stems.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Whether thou come from earth or from the lustre of the lofty heaven, Wax stronger in thy body through my song of praise: fill full all creatures, O most Wise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For India press the Soma out, most gladdening and most excellent. May Sakra make it swell sent forth with every prayer and asking, as it were, for strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let me not, still beseeching thee with earnest song at Soma rites, Anger thee like soma wild beast. Who would not beseech him who hath power to grant his prayer?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The draught made swift with rapturous joy, effectual with its mighty strength, All-conquering, distilling transport, let him drink: for he in ecstasy gives us gifts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Where bliss is not, may he, All-praised, God whom the pious glorify, Bestow great wealth upon the mortal worshipper who sheds the juice and praises him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come, Indra, and rejoice thyself, O God, in manifold affluence. Thou fillest like a lake thy vast capacious bulk with Soma and with draughts besides.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A thousand and a hundred Steeds are harnessed to thy golden car. So may the long-maned Bays, yoked by devotion, bring Indra to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Yoked to thy chariot wrought of gold, may thy two Bays with peacock tails, Convey thee hither, Steeds with their white backs, to quaff sweet juice that makes us eloquent.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So drink, thou Lover of the Song, as the first drinker, of this juice. This the outpouring of the savoury sap prepared is good and meet to gladden thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who alone by wondrous deed is Mighty, Strong by holy works, May he come, fair of cheek; may he not stay afar, but come and turn not from our call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Susna's quick moving castle thou hast crushed to pieces with thy bolts. Thou, Indra, from of old, hast followed after light, since we have had thee to invoke.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: My praises when the Sun hath risen, my praises at the time of noon, My praises at the coming of the gloom of night, O Vasu, have gone forth to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Praise yea, praise him. Of princes these are the most liberal of their gifts, These, Paramajya, Ninditasva, Prapathi, most bounteous, O Medhyatithi.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When to the car, by faith, I yoked the horses longing for the way- For skilled is Yadu's son in dealing precious wealth, he who is rich in herds of kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he who gave me two brown steeds together with their cloths of gold, May he, Asanga's son Svanadratha, obtain all joy and high felicities.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Playoga's son Asanga, by ten thousand, O Agni, hath surpassed the rest in giving. For me ten bright-hued oxen have come forward like lotus-stalks from out a lake upstanding.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What time her husband's perfect restoration to his lost strength and manhood was apparent, His consort Sasvati with joy addressed him, Now art thou well, my lord, and shalt be happy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: HERE is the Soma juice expressed; O Vasu, drink till thou art full: Undaunted God, we give it thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Washed by the men, pressed out with stones, strained through the filter made of wool, 'Tis like a courser bathed in stream.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This juice have we made sweet for thee like barley, blending it with milk. Indra, I call thee to our feast.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beloved of all, Indra alone drinks up the flowing Soma juice Among the Gods and mortal men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Friend, whom not the brilliant-hued, the badly-mixt or bitter draught, Repels, the far-extending God;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: While other men than we with milk chase him as hunters chase a deer, And with their kine inveigle him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For him, for Indra, for the God, be pressed three draughts of Soma juice In the juice-drinker's own abode.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Three reservoirs exude their drops, filled are three beakers to the brim, All for one offering to the God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pure art thou, set in many a place, and blended in the midst with milk And curd, to cheer the Hero best.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here, Indra, are thy Soma-draughts pressed out by us, the strong, the pure: They crave admixture of the milk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Indra, pour in milk, prepare the cake, and mix the Soma-draught. I hear them say that thou art rich.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Quaffed juices fight within the breast. The drunken praise not by their wine, The naked praise not when it rains.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich be the praiser of one rich, munificent and famed like thee: High rank be his, O Lord of Bays.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Foe of the man who adds no milk, he heeds not any chanted hymn Or holy psalm that may he sung.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Give us not, Indra, as a prey unto the scornful or the proud: Help, Mighty One, with power and might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This, even this, O Indra, we implore. as thy devoted friends, The Kanvas praise thee with their hymns.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Naught else, O Thunderer, have I praised in the skilled singer's eulogy: On thy land only have I thought.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Gods seek him who presses out the Soma; they desire not sleep They punish sloth unweariedly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come hither swift with gifts of wealth - be not thou angry with us-like A great man with a youthful bride.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let him not, wrathful with us, spend the evening far from us to-day, Like some unpleasant son-in-law.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For well we know this Hero's love, most liberal of the boons he gives, His plans whom the three worlds display.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pour forth the gift which Kanvas bring, for none more glorious do we know Than the Strong Lord with countless aids.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O presser, offer Soma first to Indra, Hero, Sakra, him The Friend of man, that he may drink;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who, in untroubled ways, is best provider, for his worshippers. Of strength in horses and in kine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pressers, for him blend Soma juice, each draught most excellent, for him The Brave, the Hero, for his joy.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Vrtra-slayer drinks the juice. May he who gives a hundred aids Approach, nor stay afar from us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the strong Bay Steeds, yoked by prayer, bring hither unto us our Friend, Lover of Song, renowned by songs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sweet are the Soma juices, come! Blent are the Soma juices, come! Rsi-like, mighty, fair of cheek, come hither quickly to the feast.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And lauds which strengthen thee for great bounty and valour, and exalt Indra who doeth glorious deeds,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And songs to thee who lovest song, and all those hymns addressed to thee- These evermore confirm thy might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thus he, sole doer of great deeds whose hand holds thunder, gives us strength, He who hath never been subdued.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vrtra he slays with his right hand, even Indra, great with mighty power, And much-invoked in many a place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He upon whom all men depend, all regions, all achievements, he Takes pleasure in our wealthy chiefs.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: All this hath he accomplished, yea, Indra, most gloriously renowned, Who gives our wealthy princes strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who drives his chariot seeking spoil, from afar, to him he loves: For swift is he to bring men wealth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Sage who, winning spoil with steeds, slays Vrtra, Hero with the men, His servant's faithful succourer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Priyamedhas, worship with collected mind this Indra whom The Soma hath full well inspired.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Kanvas, sing the Mighty One, Lord of the Brave, who loves renown, All-present, glorified by song.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Strong Friend, who, with no trace of feet, restores the cattle to the men, Who rest their wish and hope on him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Shaped as a Ram, Stone-hurler I once thou camest hither to the son Of Kanva, wise Medhyatithi.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Vibhindu, thou hast helped this man, giving him thousands four times ten, And afterward eight thousand more.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: And these twain pouring streams of milk, creative, daughters of delight, For wedlock sake I glorify.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: DRINK, Indra, of the savoury juice, and cheer thee with our milky draught. Be, for our weal, our Friend and sharer of the feast, and let thy wisdom guard us well.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In thy kind grace and favour may we still be strong: expose us not to foe's attack. With manifold assistance guard and succour us, and bring us to felicity.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May these my songs of praise exalt thee, Lord, who hast abundant wealth. Men skilled in holy hymns, pure, with the hues of fire, have sung them with their lauds to thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He, with his might enhanced by Rsis thousand fold, hath like an ocean spread himself. His majesty is praised as true at solemn rites, his power where holy singers rule.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra for worship of the Gods, Indra while sacrifice proceeds, Indra, as worshippers in battle-shock, we call, Indra that we may win the spoil.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With might hath Indra spread out heaven and earth, with power hath Indra lighted up the Sun. In Indra are all creatures closely held; in him meet the distilling Soma-drops.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men with their lauds are urging thee, Indra, to drink the Soma first. The Rbhus in accord have lifted up their voice, and Rudras sung thee as the first.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra increased his manly strength at sacrifice, in the wild rapture of this juice. And living men to-day, even as of old, sing forth their praises to his majesty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I crave of thee that hero strength, that thou mayst first regard this prayer, Wherewith thou holpest Bhrgu and the Yatis and Praskanva when the prize was staked.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith thou sentest mighty waters to the sea, that, Indra, is thy manly strength. For ever unattainable is this power of him to whom the worlds have cried aloud.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Help us, O Indra, when we pray to thee for wealth and hero might. First help thou on to strength the man who strives to win, and aid our laud, O Ancient One.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Help for us, Indra, as thou holpest Paura once, this man's devotions bent on gain. Help, as thou gavest Rugama and Syavaka and Svarnara and Krpa aid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What newest of imploring prayers shall, then, the zealous mortal sing? For have not they who laud his might, and Indra-power won for themselves the light of heaven?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When shall they keep the Law and praise thee mid the Gods? Who counts as Rsi and as sage? When ever wilt thou, Indra Maghavan, come nigh to presser's or to praiser's call?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These songs of ours exceeding sweet, these hymns of praise ascend to thee, Like ever-conquering chariots that display their strength, gain wealth, and give unfailing aid.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bhrgus are like Suns, like Kanvas, and have gained all that their thoughts were bent upon. The living men of Priyamedha's race have sung exalting Indra with their lauds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Best slayer of the Vrtras, yoke thy Bay Steeds, Indra, from afar. Come with the High Ones hither, Maghavan, to us, Mighty, to drink the Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For these, the bards and singers, have cried out to thee with prayer, to gain the sacrifice. As such, O Maghavan, Indra, who lovest song, even as a lover bear my call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou from the lofty plains above, O Indra, hurledst Vrtra down. Thou dravest forth the kine of guileful Mrgaya and Arbuda from the mountain's hold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bright were the flaming fires, the Sun gave forth his shine, and Soma, Indra's juice, shone clear. Indra, thou blewest the great Dragon from the air -. men must regard that valorous deed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The fairest courser of them all, who runneth on as 'twere to heaven. Which Indra and the Maruts gave, and Pakasthaman Kaurayan.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To me hath Pakasthaman given, a ruddy horse, good at the pole, Filling is girth and rousing wealth;
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Compared with whom no other ten strong coursers, harnessed to the pole, Bear Tugrya to his dwelling place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Raiment is body, food is life, and healing ointment giveth strength. As the free-handed giver of the ruddy steed, I have named Pakasthaman fourth.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOUGH, Indra, thou art called by men eastward and westward, north and south, Thou chiefly art with Anava and Turvasa, brave Champion I urged by men to Come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Or, Indra, when with Ruma, Rusama, Syavaka, and Krpa thou rejoicest thee, Still do the Kanvas, bringing praises, with their prayers, O Indra, draw thee hither: come.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Even as the wild-bull, when he thirsts, goes to the desert's watery pool, Come hither quickly both at morning and at eve, and with the Kanvas drink thy fill.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May the drops gladden thee, rich Indra, and obtain bounty for him who pours the juice. Soma pressed in the mortar didst thou take and drink, and hence hast won surpassing might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With mightier strength he conquered strength, with energy he crushed their wrath. O Indra, Strong in youth, all those who sought the fray bent and bowed down to thee like trees.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who wins promise of thine aid goes girt as with a thousand mighty men of war. He makes his son preeminent in hero might - he serves with reverential prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With thee, the Mighty, for our Friend, we will riot fear or feel fatigue. May we see Turvasa and Yadu: thy great deed, O Hero, must be glorified.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On his left hip the Hero hath reclined himself: the proffered feast offends him not. The milk is blended with the honey of the bee: quickly come hither, baste, and drink.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Indra, thy friend is fair of form and rich in horses, cars, and kine. He evermore hath food accompanied by wealth, and radiant joins the company.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come like a thirsty antelope to the drinking-place: drink Soma to thy heart's desire. Raining it down, O Maghavan, day after day, thou gainest thy surpassing might.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Priest, let the Soma juice flow forth, for Indra longs to drink thereof. He even now hath yoked his vigorous Bay Steeds: the Vrtra-slayer hath come near.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The man with whom thou fillest thee with Soma deems himself a pious worshipper. This thine appropriate food is here poured out for thee: come, hasten forward. drink of it,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Press out the Soma juice, ye priests, for Indra borne upon his car. The pressing-stones speak loud of Indra, while they shed the juice which, offered, honours him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To the brown juice may his dear vigorous Bay Steeds bring Indra, to our holy task. Hither let thy Car-steeds who seek the sacrifice bring thee to our drink-offerings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan, the Lord of ample wealth, for firm alliance we elect. May he with wisdom, Sakra! Looser! Much-invoked! aid us to riches and to seed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Sharpen us like a razor in the barber's hands: send riches thou who settest free. Easy to find with thee are treasures of the Dawn for mortal man whom thou dost speed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Pusan, I long to win thy love, I long to praise thee, Radiant God. Excellent Lord, 'tis strange tome, no wish have I to sing the psalm that Pajra sings.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: My kine, O Radiant God, seek pasture where they will, my during wealth, Immortal One. Be our protector, Pusan! be, most liberal Lord, propitious to our gathering strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Rich was the gift Kurunga gave, a hundred steeds at morning rites. Among the gifts of Turvasas we thought of him, the opulent, the splendid King.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What by his morning songs Kanva, the powerful, hath, with the Priyamedhas, gained- The herds of sixty thousand pure and spotless kine, have I, the Rsi, driven away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The very trees were joyful at my coming: kine they obtained in plenty, steeds in plenty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WHEN, even as she were present here, red Dawn hath shone from far away, She spreadeth light on every side.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like Heroes on your will-yoked car far shining, Wonder-Workers! ye Attend, O Asvins, on the Dawn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By you, O Lords of ample wealth our songs of praise have been observed: As envoy have I brought the prayer.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Kanvas must praise the Asvins dear to many, making many glad, Most rich, that they may succour us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Most liberal, best at winning strength, inciters, Lords of splendour who Visit the worshipper's abode.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: So for devout Sudeva dew with fatness his unfailing mead, And make it rich for sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hitherward running speedily with horses, as with rapid hawks, Come, Asvins, to our song of praise
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Wherewith the three wide distances, and all the lights that are in heaven. Ye traverse, and three times of night.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Finders of the Day, that we may win us food of kine and wealth, Open the paths for us to tread.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Asvins, bring us wealth in kine, in noble heroes, and in cars: Bring us the strength that horses give.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Lords of splendour, glorified, ye Wonder-Workers borne on paths Of gold, drink sweets with Soma juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To us, ye Lords of ample wealth, and to our wealth chiefs extend Wide shelter, ne'er to be assailed.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come quickly downward to the prayer of people whom ye favour most: Approach not unto other folk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye Asvins whom our minds perceive, drink of this lovely gladdening draught, The meath which we present to you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring riches hither unto us in hundreds and in thousands, source Of plenteous food, sustaining all.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Verily sages call on you, ye Heroes, in full many a place. Moved by the priests, O Asvins, conic.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Men who have trimmed the sacred grass, bringing oblations and prepared, O Asvins, are invoking you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May this our hymn of praise to-day, most powerful to bring you, be, O Asvins, nearest to your hearts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The skin filled full of savoury meath, laid in the pathway of your car- O Asvins, drink ye both therefrom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: For this, ye Lords of ample wealth, bring blessing for our herd, our kine, Our progeny, and plenteous food.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye too unclose to us like doors the strengthening waters of the sky, And rivers, ye who find the day.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When did the son of' Tugra serve you, Men? Abandoned in the sea, That with winged steeds your car might fly.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Ye, O Nasatyas, ministered to Kanva with repeated aid, When cast into the heated pit.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
